newsitem.title: UK: LME copper adopts firmer tone after stock drop.
newsitem.headline: LME copper adopts firmer tone after stock drop.

text.p: A bigger than expected drawdown in London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks gave copper prices a gentle boost on Friday morning.
The inventory report also held surprises for tin, which came off sharply after a stocks rise. Moderate drawdowns in aluminium and zinc extracted cooler reactions than in copper.
Three months copper edged up from firmer morning levels after the stocks showed a decline of 9,675 tonnes.
It was last at $2,360 per tonne, compared to Thursday's constructive kerb close of $2,351.50.
"People were expecting up to 7,000 tonnes down, so it was slightly more than expected and gave some $3/$4 to the price," a trader said.
If Thursday's momentum continued building copper could expect to test the $2,375 resistance level, dealers and analysts said.
Aluminium prices were slightly easier after a stock drop of 5,525 tonnes. Prices were at $1,665 per tonne, compared to $1,669 on Thursday.
Traders attributed the lack of supportive reponse to talk early on Friday that stocks would be down a significantly higher 10,000-15,000 tonnes.
"When it came in a lot lower it put some pressure on the price," a trader said. "Plus on Thursday aluminium ran into trouble around $1,670 and maybe it's done enough for now."
Tin prices crumbled below $6,000 per tonne after stocks showed a rise of 410 tonnes, instead of an expected small drawdown, traders said.
The recent backwardation in the cash/threes may have attracted metal to LME warehouses, confounding inventory expectations, they said.
Three months tin was last at $5,965, compared to $6,025 on Thursday. The decline below $5,980 triggered stops which sent it initially to $5,950 after the stock report.
In zinc, a stock drop of 2,850 tonnes was neutralised by a bout of Chinese selling early on Friday, traders said, and prices were unchanged at $1,305.
Prices remained capped at Thursday's high of $1,307, a level which needs to be negated before resistance at $1,320 can be tackled, analysts said.
Lead was also indicated little changed at $695/$697, compared to $694, after stocks dropped by 625 tonnes as expected.
Nickel was steady at $8,030, down $10, after inventories increased by 234 tonnes.
Alloy was indicated at $1,545/55, versus $1,553. Stocks were down 200 tonnes.
